causedByTheseRepairs.clause: §0C.22-ter's ElementFor<K> (repair 6), and nameSourceOf's 'option' branch that reads it
causedByTheseRepairs.consequence: NEW, and the most serious of the set. ElementFor<'option'> = OptionItem | (OptionItem & { duration; price }) | (OptionItem & { nearest_availability }) omits StrategyOptionsBody['alternatives'][number]. §2.6.11 declares alternatives with title: Cell<string> and NO label, and its declared interactive path alternatives[].option_id produces {k:'option'} refs — the fact §0C.22-sexies was written to record. So (i) nameSourceOf's branch `('label' in el ? el.label : el.title).label` reads el.title, a member no declared alternative of ElementFor<'option'> carries — a dangling member access; (ii) resolveInteractive's return type cannot denote STRATEGY_OPTIONS's resolved element, so the function is partial over InteractiveRef's seven members and its totality claim is false; (iii) §0C.22-septies's ruling that 'an alternative's accessible name is its title verbatim' becomes unsatisfiable, and with it A-2's startsWith check for every STRATEGY_OPTIONS envelope. Secondarily, A | (A & B) reduces to A for member access, so the two selector intersections are inert for their stated purpose: under base:'element' renderSuffix's el is typed OptionItem and duration/price/nearest_availability are unreachable.
causedByTheseRepairs.fix: Restore the dropped member and make the selector fields reachable: `: K extends 'option' ? OptionItem | (OptionItem & { duration: Measure; price: Measure | null }) | (OptionItem & { nearest_availability: Cell<string> }) | StrategyOptionsBody['alternatives'][number]`. Because a union collapses for member access, also state that renderSuffix's `el` parameter is typed ElementFor<K> for the ref being named, and that each pointer is resolved by name against the resolved element's own declared members (absence refuses the envelope at EP-MINT).
